'''Origin:''' Vabbi
'''Age:''' 24
'''Profession:''' Mesmer/Actor
[[Norgu]] is a classically trained actor, a visionary unappreciated in his own time, and a large, dramatic, boisterous glad-hander. As the leader of the [[Lyssan Fools]] acting troupe, he is currently on an extended tour of the estates of [[Vabbi]]an nobles. Everywhere he travels, he leaves a memorable impression. Few will forget his insightfully accurate and delightfully humorous parody of [[General Bayel]] in [[Gandara]], a performance that should keep him on an extended tour for quite some time. Norgu claims to have traveled throughout [[Tyria]] and [[Cantha]], returning with stories of a standing-room-only performance in the court of [[Emperor Kisu]] and a standing ovation at the [[Henge of Denravi]]. Moving quickly from one region to the next, he uses his sunny disposition and personal charisma to get last-minute invites to parties, audiences with the rich and powerful, and of course, free food. Norgu never met a buffet he didn't like. Surrender!"'' :''"Your imagination is your enemy!"'' :''"Action!"'' ==Notes== *A duplicate Norgu will show up as a "Vabbian Mesmer". *Norgu's default weapon is a customized maximum damage [[Item rarity|blue]] [[Hypnotic Scepter]] with an [[attribute]] requirement of 9 [[Illusion Magic]] and [[Energy]] +5 while [[Health]] is above 50%. His default [[focus item]] is a +12 energy blue [[Jeweled Chakram]] [[of Fortitude]] with an attribute requirement of 9 Illusion Magic and Health +20. *A fellow actor, [[Tannaros]], is bitter that the Theatrical Academy considered Norgu's plans to be better than his. *As with all heroes, this one has a [[Everlasting Norgu Tonic|tonic form]]. == Trivia == * Two of his quotes are paraphrases from Shakespeare's plays: ** From ''Julius Caesar'', ''"Cowards die a thousand times..."'' ** From ''Romeo & Juliet'', the line beginning with ''"[a]nd, when he shall die..."'' ("heaven" in the original is replaced with "the mists" here). * His quote, ''"This is just like act three, scene four"'' is likely a reference to the same scene in "Hamlet" in which Hamlet himself kills Polonius. * His quote, ''"Ah, acting is happy agony..."'' paraphrases the French philosopher, Jean-Paul Sartre. == References == {{Heroes nav}}
